name: Munchables
rootCause: The Blast ecosystem project Munchables was attacked, resulting in a loss of approximately $62.5 million. On the same day, Blast founder Pacman tweeted: "$97m has been secured in a multisig by Blast core contributors. Took an incredible lift in the background but I’m grateful the ex munchables dev opted to return all funds in the end without any ransom required.."

descriptions.text: The Blast L2 Big Bang award-winning project Munchables was exploited for $62.5M by a rogue dev. Funds retrieved from dev within a few hours in a rollercoaster ride of a day.

The Blast ecosystem project Munchables was attacked, resulting in a loss of approximately $62.5 million. On the same day, Blast founder Pacman tweeted: "$97m has been secured in a multisig by Blast core contributors. Took an incredible lift in the background but I’m grateful the ex munchables dev opted to return all funds in the end without any ransom required.."

On March 26,27, 2024, an insider at Munchables manipulated proxy contract storage on Blast L2, assigning themselves a large ETH balance and withdrawing 17,413 ETH (~$62.5M). The exploit leveraged a backdoored implementation, premeditated before platform launch. Recovered private keys allowed full fund recovery to a multisig. An insider developer pre-deployed a proxy implementation with a backdoor, manipulated storage slots to assign themselves a large ETH balance, then withdrew nearly all contract funds using privileged access. Existing upgrade checks could not detect the pre-assigned balance. The design allowed dangerous upgradeability without proper verification or multi-party control.

On March 26, 2024, a developer hired by the Munchables GameFi protocol on Blast upgraded the main contract to assign themselves a massive fake ETH balance, then withdrew 17,413 ETH (~$62.8 million). The attacker surrendered the keys and all funds were recovered after public negotiation. A developer with privileged access abused upgrade rights to the protocol's proxy contract, pushing an implementation that granted themselves a fictional ETH balance. Weak internal controls allowed a single actor to deploy and upgrade contracts, enabling insider fraud.

The "Munchables" crypto game explains: "Schnibbles grow on every realm across the Munchable's world. Each realm has their own unique and distinctive schniblet, and the Munchables react differently based on their compatibility to the schniblets fed to them. When creating an account for the Munchables, you must choose the location of your snuggery." Right then. Things went awry in the land of the schnibbles and snuggeries when an attacker siphoned around 17,400 ETH ($62.5 million).
